items.title: Dalen Terry, Thunder Agree To Two-Year Contract
items.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder and veteran wing Dalen Terry have agreed to a two-year contract. Terry will fill the Thunder's open roster spot and will give the team some much needed depth. Last season, Terry split the campaign between the Chicago Bulls and Philadelphia 76ers. Terry was traded by the Bulls to the New York Knicks at the trade deadline, then he signed a two-way contract with the Sixers. From there, the 6-foot-7 wing signed a standard contract with Philadelphia. The Thunder are currently down six players due to injuries. That includes Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, who are expected to miss the remainder of the season, and Chet Holmgren who is out for 8-10 weeks.

items.title: Mike Brown On Struggling Knicks: 'We Have To Hit Singles'
items.summary: New York Knicks head coach Mike Brown said that his team has to return to playing simple after a 98-93 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday night. They are now 2-4 on the season. "We're trying to get a home run every time we get the ball," Brown said. "We have to hit singles." The Knicks shot just 40.7% from the field and 31.7% from three. Jalen Brunson added that the Knicks need to be more decisive in their play. "Sometimes it can be us being hesitant as well, wanting to make the right play," said Brunson. "We understand what we have to do, it's just starting the game that way. That has to be our biggest point of emphasis going forward." Mikel Bridges continued his early season struggles, finishing with 12 points and five rebounds. Bridges is averaging 6.2 points and 2.8 rebounds on the year. Karl-Anthony Towns echoed Brunson in saying that the team needs to improve how they start games. "I think we did a great job in the fourth quarter of finding that gear, of getting out the quicksand, finally turning gears into motion. "It puts us in position where you've got to make some magic happen, and we just didn't have enough magic today to get back and win the game," said Towns.
